recording.starts: fresh install, splash (FABULOUS 'Habit building made easy' sign-in screen with press logos)
recording.after_paywall: No exit or discount offer: X leads straight to a Duke University study claim, a first habit challenge and an app tour; a second paywall (3:36) is followed by an 'Are you sure?' interstitial, then a 60-minute welcome-gift countdown opens a gift paywall at the annual price (4:15) and an 'Unlock FABULOUS' sheet (4:22).

strategy: Fabulous sells change as a journey into a storybook world backed by 'science': it opens with press logos and a glowing doorway, has the person audit their life in quick taps, then turns a second round of taps into a personal 'tracking sheet' that feels like work already done. Name and email are framed as saving that progress, and a named contract sealed with a hold-to-commit gesture turns vague intention into a ceremonial pledge seconds before the price. The paywall then cashes in the pledge with a letter from 'future Cameron' that dates today as the turning point. The one idea carrying it is self-commitment: make the person promise themselves, by name and with their body, so subscribing reads as keeping their own word.

phases.name: Hook and threshold
phases.goal: Establish credibility (press, 'Just science') and cast the person as a traveller entering a magical world, while getting them past the sign-in gate with a nudge toward giving an account.

phases.name: Life audit
phases.goal: Get the person to reflect on sleep, energy, fitness and the habits that trouble them, surfacing a gap between how they live and how they want to live, in fast tap-to-advance questions that feel conversational.

phases.name: Build your worksheet
phases.goal: Turn quick yes/no answers about today into a tangible, shareable artifact so the person feels they have already started tracking and produced something of their own, then reward them for it.

phases.name: Save your progress
phases.goal: Collect name, age, gender, wake time and a required email under the banner of protecting progress already made, so handing over data feels like saving work rather than signing up; the name sets up the personal contract and letter.

phases.name: The contract
phases.goal: Elicit a named, physical pledge so that the next ask (payment) feels like the first act of keeping a promise just made.

phases.name: Future-self paywall
phases.goal: Convert while the pledge is fresh: a letter from the person's future self declares today the day they changed and claims the outcome, with one quarterly plan softened by a free week.

phases.name: Into the app, gifts and later paywalls
phases.goal: Reassure the person who declined with authority and a first tiny win, then keep re-presenting the upgrade in softer, gift-shaped and time-limited forms.

screens.title: Habit building made easy
screens.body: FABULOUS / Not magic. Just science. / As featured on: The New York Times, WIRED, Forbes, girlboss, healthline / By continuing, you agree to our Terms and Conditions
screens.controls: Skip (pill, top right). Buttons: Continue with Apple; Existing Users
screens.visual: Blue-to-violet gradient, FABULOUS wordmark with logo, painted arched doorway opening onto a glowing sunrise with streaking pink clouds and dark grass, row of press wordmarks in white, white Apple button and indigo Existing Users button on a dark bottom panel. No progress bar.
screens.intent: Front-loads credibility before any ask: an easy promise ('made easy'), a line that pre-empts scepticism ('Not magic. Just science.') and five press logos as borrowed authority. The open door frames the app as a threshold into a new life, and the trust signals sit exactly where the person decides whether to give an account.

screens.title: Are you sure?
screens.body: Verifying your email is highly recommended.
screens.controls: Buttons: Go Back; Skip
screens.visual: White bottom sheet over the dimmed splash, crimson title, large crimson Go Back button, Skip as faint grey text below. The person taps Skip and onboarding continues without sign-in.
screens.intent: Adds friction and a hint of risk to skipping sign-in: the coloured primary action is to go back, while Skip is visually demoted. Mild pressure aimed at capturing identity early.

screens.body: Enter the Fabulous world, where you will turn your intentions into reality
screens.controls: None (auto-advances after about 8 seconds)
screens.visual: Dark aubergine screen, small isometric purple pyramid with a glowing door and blue sparkles, the app's tiny white cloaked traveller walking toward it; small grey caption near the bottom. Ends with a circular iris wipe to black (0:12).
screens.intent: Slows the person down and casts them as a traveller entering a world, so what follows feels like a quest rather than a form. The line names the problem the app sells against (intentions that never become reality) without asking anything yet.

screens.title: Create the perfect routine for you
screens.body: Using psychology and behavioral science you will create healthy habits that stick
screens.controls: Button: Let's Get Started
screens.visual: Painted full moon (or low sun) over a path through dark grass with fireflies; headline fades in at the top, caption and pink pill button at the bottom. Dissolves into the bright painted landscape of the quiz.
screens.intent: States the deliverable (a personal routine) and the method (behavioural science) just before the quiz, so every following answer is read as input into 'the perfect routine for you'. Repeats the science claim to keep authority high.

screens.visual: Same landscape; cards and title cross-fade; traveller and bird shift slightly between questions.
screens.intent: The 'Got it!' prefix acknowledges the previous answer, making the quiz feel like a conversation without a separate validation screen.

screens.title: Let's analyze your current habits
screens.body: Before building your new routine, let's create your personalized tracking sheet to take stock of how well you are doing
screens.controls: Button: Let's Go
screens.visual: World changes from the painted landscape to a soft lilac-blue gradient. A tilted, blank 'MY MENTAL HEALTH tracking sheet' floats with sparkles (To-Do List, Water Balance, Morning Routine: Meditation, Breakfast, Vitamins, Things I am Grateful for Today, Hours of Sleep, Productivity stars, Mood faces). Blue button at the bottom.
screens.intent: Marks a shift from 'who you are' to 'what you did today' and shows the empty artifact the next questions will fill, so each answer feels like completing one's own sheet. 'Personalized' and 'take stock' promise a mirror and a check-up, and 'Before building your new routine' keeps the routine as the pending reward.

screens.title: MY MENTAL HEALTH tracking sheet
screens.body: To-Do List: Values alignment / Water Balance: / Morning Routine: Meditation Breakfast Vitamins / Things I am Grateful for Today: / Hours of Sleep: 0-3 4-6 7-9 10-12 / Productivity: / Mood: / Tap Anywhere to Continue
screens.controls: Tap anywhere to continue. Button: Share My worksheet. X (top right)
screens.visual: On black, the sheet slides up as a card with the Fabulous logo. Answers are written in one at a time in a handwriting style: 'Values alignment' appears on the To-Do List, one water glass fills blue, a tick is drawn next to Breakfast. 'Tap Anywhere to Continue' sits on a dark fade at the bottom with a white share pill below. The person taps on at 1:53 before the remaining tiles visibly fill.
screens.intent: Converts nine low-effort taps into a tangible artifact in what looks like their own handwriting, so the person feels they have already started tracking and that the app now 'knows' their day. The share button invites public commitment and free word of mouth.

screens.title: Congratulations!
screens.body: Track many more habits, and create healthy routines from within your Fabulous account.
screens.controls: Button: Continue
screens.visual: Lilac-blue gradient, the tilted worksheet with sparkles (shown as the blank template again, not the filled version), title fades in at the top, blue button at the bottom.
screens.intent: Rewards completing what was really a short survey, then pivots: more tracking lives 'within your Fabulous account', which tees up name and email capture as the way to keep what was just made.

screens.title: Your email (required)

screens.visual: Royal blue, back arrow, keyboard with the iOS suggested address and Hide My Email; Continue turns white once filled. The opt-out radio is off by default.
screens.intent: Makes email mandatory after several minutes of investment, so leaving now would mean losing the worksheet; marketing emails are on unless the person opts out.

screens.title: Cameron's Contract
screens.body: I, Cameron, will make the most of tomorrow. I will always remember that I will not live forever. Every fear and irritation that threatens to distract me will become fuel for building my best life one day at a time. / Hint: tap and hold to commit. Precommiting to a goal (via contracts like this) has been shown to inspire action and reduce procrastination.
screens.controls: Hold button (orange circle with a fingerprint). Labels while holding: Hold it; Almost there; Nice! Good luck with the challenge!
screens.visual: Royal blue over the painted alchemist's desk. The contract types itself out letter by letter (2:17 to about 2:28), then the hint and the orange fingerprint button appear. Holding grows the orange circle from 'Hold it' (2:31) through 'Almost there' (2:32) to 'Nice! Good luck with the challenge!' (2:33) until it floods the screen, then an orange wipe into the paywall (2:35).
screens.intent: The emotional peak right before price: the person's name in a formal oath, a memento mori line that raises the stakes, and a research-flavoured hint that justifies the ritual. Holding for several seconds makes commitment bodily and effortful, so the paywall that follows reads as the first test of the promise; declining is made to feel like breaking one's own word.

screens.subtype: future-self letter, single plan, free trial
screens.title: Cameron, do you copy?
screens.body: It’s me, future Cameron. I’m calling from 2027 because today is an important day for you —for us. / Tuesday, September 29, 2026 is the day we decided to change our lives for the better. / I have excellent news: I’m healthy, in great shape, and worry-free, thanks to the choices you’re making. / I’ll be with you every step of the way. / See you soon, Future Cameron / Get Fabulous Premium Membership Billed every 3 months 39.99 USD /quarter / Terms & Conditions | Privacy Policy / You won't be charged until after your free week ends.
screens.controls: X (top left, visible from the first frame). Button: JOIN FREE FOR A WEEK (inside the offer card). Links: Terms & Conditions; Privacy Policy. After the tap: toast 'Fabulous choice! Just a moment...' and a sticky bottom bar with Buy Now / Try free for 7 days
screens.visual: Dark aubergine background, gold coin with the Fabulous triangle logo, centred white letter with a bold date paragraph and italic sign-off; magenta-to-crimson offer card over a space illustration (red cube, white triangles, tiny traveller on a floating island, orange planet) with a white pill CTA. The person scrolls to the CTA (2:41 to 2:46), taps it (2:47), closes the Apple sheet, scrolls back to the top and taps X at 2:53.
screens.intent: Cashes in the contract: a letter 'from 2027' signed by the person's future self names today as the turning point and asserts the outcome already happened, so paying is framed as honouring that self. Only one plan is shown (quarterly) with a free week and a no-charge line to remove risk. The guaranteed-outcome testimony from 'yourself' is a strong, misleading promise and the dated 'today' adds quiet urgency.

screens.title: Cameron's First Step
screens.body: A Duke University study states that people who used Fabulous were more likely to achieve their goals, stay motivated, and feel better about themselves in 2 weeks. / Now, it's your turn.
screens.controls: Buttons: Continue; Let me explore first
screens.visual: 2:54 to 3:12. No discount or exit offer after X. 'Cameron's First Step' over a low-poly purple mountain with the traveller at the summit; then the mascot says 'I'll remind you to build your habits!' with 'Remind me about habits' / 'No, I'll do this on my own' (3:01, a reminder primer); a story card 'An Unexpected Journey' ('In which Cameron intentionally designs each morning for a bright today and a brighter tomorrow.'); the first challenge 'Drink Water' ('This week, drink water as soon as you wake up. You're hydrating your body and, just as importantly, you're demonstrating follow-through.', 'Do it 3 times this week to succeed', 'I accept the challenge', 'Embarking in 3 seconds...').
screens.intent: Replaces a discount with authority and a first tiny win: an uncited university study claim reassures the person who just declined, then a one-habit challenge gives an immediate, easy success.

screens.subtype: app tour, second paywall, 'Are you sure?' interstitial
screens.title: Journeys
screens.body: The Mountains / Welcome to Fabulous! Mountains are cornerstones to build your Fabulous self. Adventure through 3 levels to master these Mountains.
screens.controls: Coach-mark arrows; tour taps
screens.visual: 3:12 to 4:06. Journeys map tour with coach marks (First Mountain - The Foundation, Second Mountain - The Struggle, Third Mountain - The Fountain, The Return). At 3:36 a second paywall, 'Start your journey to better living.' (lighthouse painting, X top left, crimson lower panel not yet loaded), is closed within about 2 seconds and followed by a red 'Are you sure?' interstitial with a painted smartwatch (3:38). Then a Routines tour ('Welcome Cameron! This is your Wake Up Routine...', 'Just tap on the checkbox to mark it as done. Give it a try!'), an 'Easy!' celebration card, Home with a red Upgrade pill and 'Letter no. 1' ('Welcome, Cameron, to a journey that will take you behind the scenes of human behavior...'), a reminder pledge 'You are all set!' ('Cameron, are you going to Drink Water tomorrow?' Yes, I Will! / No, I Am Not Yet Ready), an 'OK, got it!' feedback ask, and 'Let's do it!' (Embark On Your Journey).
screens.intent: Keeps the quest framing going with small, celebrated actions and another named pledge, while a second paywall and a guilt-tinged 'Are you sure?' screen test the person again after a short tour.

screens.subtype: reward, countdown gift paywall, Unlock sheet
screens.title: Cameron, here is a Streak Freeze! You've earned it.
screens.body: You can use it to skip a day without losing your Streak.
screens.controls: Button: Equip for Free
screens.visual: 4:06 to 4:28. Magic-hat animation and the mascot holding a blue crystal on a starry blue screen. Home then shows a floating 'Claim your welcome gift 00:59:59' countdown banner with Yes. Gift paywall at 4:15: 'We appreciate you, Cameron!' over a gift box on teal, 'Set your custom goals, and let us guide you towards them. Start with 7 days free, then continue at a discounted price. Cancel anytime.', Accept Gift; its Apple sheet reads 'Fabulous Premium ... 1-week free trial ... $39.99 per year, Starting Oct 6, 2026' (closed). At 4:22 the Upgrade pill opens an 'Unlock FABULOUS' sheet: 'Enjoy your first week, it's free!', four ticked benefits ('Achieve any habit you want', 'Get unstuck', 'Finally own a positive mindset', 'Make success inevitable'), boxed renewal terms, 'Try 7 Days for Free', Continue, 'One week free, then 39.99 USD /year'. Recording ends in Control Center at 4:27.
screens.intent: Reciprocity, then urgency: an 'earned' reward primes goodwill, a one-hour countdown frames the annual plan as an expiring gift, and the same $39.99 now buys a year instead of a quarter, which retroactively makes the first paywall's price the high anchor.

intermission_pattern: Fabulous uses few stand-alone intermissions (6 against 21 questions) and places them only at section boundaries, never inside a question block: three up front (press splash, animated world intro, promise screen), a section intro that previews the worksheet, a reveal plus 'Congratulations!' after the worksheet questions, and the contract right before the paywall. Inside the blocks it replaces validation screens with one or two word acknowledgements written into the next question's title ('Got it!', 'Understood!', 'We hear you.'), and it carries continuity through art rather than words: one painted landscape with a cloaked traveller for the life audit, then corner illustrations in the second block that match the tiles of the worksheet being filled. The tone is storybook and aspirational, text is short, and 'science' is asserted rather than shown (no stats, charts, loaders or plan-building), the only research reference before the paywall being the contract's precommitment hint. Collectively the intermissions build a ritual arc (enter a world, produce a personal artifact, sign a named oath) so the paywall reads as the next step of a promise rather than a sales screen.
standouts: Screen 30 turns commitment into a physical act: a contract in the person's name, with a memento mori line and a research-flavoured hint about precommitment, is sealed by holding a button that swells to fill the screen ('Hold it', 'Almost there', 'Nice! Good luck with the challenge!') seconds before the price.

Screen 23 converts nine yes/no taps into a handwritten, shareable 'MY MENTAL HEALTH tracking sheet', giving the person a tangible artifact and the sense that tracking has already begun, and screen 24 celebrates it with 'Congratulations!' before routing straight to name and email.

Screen 31 takes mirroring to its extreme: a letter from 'future Cameron' dated today claims the transformation already happened ('I’m healthy, in great shape, and worry-free'), an outcome promise disguised as self-testimony.

Screens 6, 8 and 11 show a cheap alternative to validation screens: a short acknowledgement ('Got it!', 'Understood!', 'We hear you.') prefixed to the next question keeps the quiz conversational without adding a screen.
gaps: The person stays on screen 12 for about 29 seconds (0:44 to 1:13) with no other screens in between. The worksheet reveal (screen 23) was tapped through before its fill animation finished, so it is unclear whether every answer would have been written in; only the to-do item, one water glass and the Breakfast tick were seen. The account email on the Apple sheet (screen 32) and the typed email (screen 29) are personal data and are not transcribed. Curly versus straight apostrophes cannot be told apart reliably on some lines. The number on the smartwatch in the post-paywall 'Are you sure?' interstitial (3:38) is not clearly legible. Everything after 2:54 is summarised in three app entries, as instructed. Counts: 'other' is 2 account, 2 paywall and 3 app entries. No new mechanism names were added.
